correctness.rationale: For standard Δ_{n,k}, n>=5 and 2<=k<=n-2, intrinsic normals lie in the zero-sum hyperplane. Sorting a normal u, the width is its largest r-coordinate sum minus smallest r-coordinate sum, r=min(k,n-k). Every ordered mean-zero u is a nonnegative sum of centered two-level gap rays v^(j). On this chamber width is linear, and the Euclidean triangle inequality proves W=min_j min(r,j,n-j)√[n/(j(n-j))]; strictness excludes multiray equality. Monotonicity in j leaves only j=1 and balanced floor(n/2), giving W=min{√[n/(n-1)], r√[n/(floor(n/2)ceil(n/2))]}. Exact parity algebra yields singleton direction below n=4r²-1, balanced above, and BOTH only at that odd integer. Independently enumerated every rational candidate ray minimum and exact phase for all n=5..170 and admissible r (7225 cases); these finite checks supplement the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: Har-Peled and Robson (2023) give complete Euclidean width for REGULAR SIMPLICES (rank one), outside the new 2<=k<=n-2 range. Martínez-Sandoval and Padrol (2019) concern projections and skeletons of hypersimplices, not intrinsic minimum width. Connected-matroid-base-polytope inradius already implies the centrally symmetric special case n=2k, which is acknowledged prior. Neither establishes the nonsymmetric all-rank formula or precise all-minimizing-normal quadratic transition.
residual_risks: An unindexed hypersimplex thickness or Ky Fan spread inequality might give a stronger all-rank bound.
Only intrinsic Euclidean normals are meaningful; ambient normals would give trivial zero width.
